title: Studying the Stoichiometry of Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor in Intact Cells using Correlative Microscopy
protocol: Prepare labeling buffer (BSA-GEL-PBS) using autoclaved phosphate buffered saline, pH 7.4 (PBS).
Supplement labeling buffer with 1% BSA and 0.2% gelatin.
Vortex or shake the labeling buffer well.
Store labeling buffer for up to 5 days at 4 °C.
Prepare washing buffer (BSA-PBS) from autoclaved phosphate buffered saline, pH 7.4.
Supplement washing buffer with 1% BSA.
Vortex or shake the washing buffer well.
Store washing buffer for up to 5 days at 4 °C.
Prepare 50 mM borate buffer (BB) from a 200 mM boric acid stock solution, adjusting pH to 8.3 with sodium tetraborate.
Store borate buffer for up to 12 months at 4 °C.
Prepare 0.1 M cacodylate buffer (CB) from a 0.2 M sodium cacodylate stock solution, adjusting pH to 7.4 and supplementing with 0.1 M sucrose.
Store opened cacodylate buffer for up to 5 days at 4 °C.
Prepare 0.1 M glycine in PBS (GLY-PBS).
Store glycine-PBS for up to 2 months at 4 °C.
Prepare 3% paraformaldehyde in CB (3% PFA) from a freshly made or opened vial of 16% PFA, EM grade.
Store opened 3% PFA solution for up to 5 days at 4 °C.
Prepare 2% glutaraldehyde in CB (2% GA) from a freshly made or opened vial of 25% GA stock solution, EM grade.
Store opened 2% GA solution for up to 5 days at 4 °C.
Dilute 6 µM EGF-biotin stock solution in BSA-GEL-PBS to create a 300 nM EGF-biotin labeling solution.
Use the diluted EGF-biotin solution within a few hours.
Centrifuge the streptavidin-QD stock solution for 4 min at 8,000 x g.
Take the supernatant and dilute it 1:10 in BB.
Use different types of QDs (e.g., QD655 or QD800) as needed.
Dilute to a final concentration in BSA-GEL-PBS using 75-100 μl per microchip.
Prepare 10 nM STR-QD labeling solution.
Clean a microscope glass slide with a clean room tissue and HPLC grade ethanol.
Open a 100 mm diameter Petri dish, and lay the cleaned microscope glass into the dish; leave the dish open.
Use clean tweezers to take 4-10 microchips with thin (50 nm) silicon nitride membranes out of their storage box onto the glass slide.
Grip the microchips gently at their sides without touching the fragile upper side, consisting of the thin silicon nitride membrane.
Close the lid of the petri dish and bring it to a fume hood.
Get a new clean room tissue and deposit it beside the petri dish.
Prepare two clean 200 ml glass beakers by filling one with 50-70 ml acetone, and the other with a similar volume of ethanol, both of HPLC grade.
Transfer the microchips from the glass slide first onto the clean room tissue.
Transfer microchips from the tissue into the acetone-filled beaker to remove the protective resist layer.
Wait 2 min while gently moving the beaker a few times to ensure that the microchips are well rinsed.
Transfer the microchips directly into the ethanol-filled beaker, without letting them dry out.
Wait 2 min in the ethanol beaker.
Transfer the beaker with microchips to the laminar airflow workbench.
Get a new clean room tissue and transfer the chips onto it to let them dry for a few minutes.
Transfer the dried microchips back onto the glass slide in the Petri dish.
Close the lid of the petri dish, and bring it to the plasma cleaner.
Deposit the glass slide with the microchips into the plasma cleaner.
Run a 5 min cleaning program using settings of 70 mTorr, gas flow of 11.5 sccm for O2 and 35.0 sccm for Ar, 50 W forward radio frequency (RF) target, and 5 W RF range with max reflected RF.
Put the glass slide with microchips back into the petri dish after plasma cleaning.
Close the lid of the petri dish to keep the microchips sterile from now on.
Examine the window areas of the microchips under a light microscope for possible membrane ruptures or remaining dirt particles.
Bring the petri dish to the laminar airflow workbench.

Place tubes/bottles containing sterilized 0.01% poly-L-lysine solution, HPLC grade water, Dulbecco's Modified Eagle Medium (DMEM) supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum, DMEM without serum, a new clean room tissue, a sterile 24-well plate, a sterile 96-well plate, sterile pipet tips, a pipette, and flat, rounded tip tweezers on the workbench.
Fill one well of the 24-well plate with PLL using an approximate volume of 1 ml.
Fill two wells of the 24-well plate with HPLC grade water using an approximate volume of 1 ml per well.
Briefly flame and cool off the tips of the tweezers to sterilize them.
Transfer microchips from the glass slide onto the clean room tissue using the sterile tweezers.
Transfer up to six microchips into the PLL-filled well in the 24-well plate.
Incubate the microchips for 5 minutes.
Rinse the microchips by placing them, one-by-one, into the first water-filled well.
Transfer the rinsed microchips from the first water-filled well to the second water-filled well.
Do not leave the microchips in the water longer than about a minute.
Place each rinsed microchip individually into the DMEM-filled wells of the 96-well plate.
Store the 96-well plate in the CO2 incubator until the cell suspension is prepared.
Subculture COS7 cells to prepare a cell suspension with a concentration of approximately 5 × 10^5 cells/ml.
Ensure that the cells are mono-dispersed in the suspension.
Add one droplet of cell suspension to each microchip in the 96-well plate.
Wait for 5 minutes after adding the cell suspension to each microchip.
Examine the window areas of the microchips with an inverted microscope to choose the right moment for transfer.
Transfer the microchip into a new well containing serum-free DMEM when sufficient cells have adhered onto the window.
Maintain the microchips with the cells facing up and avoid touching this side during handling.
Examine each microchip window after transfer.
Re-trititerate the cell suspension if too many cells are washed off and the number of remaining cells is insufficient.
Repeat steps 3.1-3.5 if necessary to ensure an adequate number of adhering cells on each microchip.
Transfer all microchips with sufficient cells into a well containing serum-free DMEM.
Place the 96-well plate back into the CO2 incubator for cell recovery and flattening overnight.
Rinse microchips by placing them in a well with fresh BSA-GEL-PBS.
Incubate microchips in BSA-GEL-PBS at 37°C for 5 minutes.
Place the 96-well plate back into the incubator after rinsing.
Incubate cells with 300 nM EGF-biotin solution for 3 minutes at 37°C.
Rinse microchips three times with PBS and once with cold buffer (CB).
Incubate in 3% paraformaldehyde (PFA) for 10 minutes.
Rinse chips once with CB, then rinse three times with PBS.
Incubate in glycerol-PBS for 2 minutes.
Rinse microchips twice with PBS.
Incubate in 10 nM streptavidin quantum dots (STR-QD) for 10 minutes.
Rinse chips four times with BSA-PBS.
Submerge a microchip in a glass-bottom 35 mm dish pre-filled with BSA-PBS at room temperature.
Acquire differential interference contrast (DIC) images of QD-labeled cells.
Use a 40X air objective for overview images of cells labeled with QD655.
Use an oil immersion objective to collect emitted fluorescence light from cells labeled with QD800.
Select a filter cube that exposes QDs to fluorescence excitation light between 340 and 380 nm, collecting emitted light above 420 nm.
Minimize the light intensity to avoid sample damage.
Set the exposure time to at least 300 msec for signal capture of all QDs.
Adjust the light intensity and amplification for bright images without visible noise while minimizing light intensity.
Place the imaged microchip back into a well of a 96-well plate filled with BSA-PBS, cells facing up.
Rinse microchips once in CB.
Incubate in 2% GA for 10 min.
Rinse microchips once in CB.
Rinse microchips three times with BSA-PBS.
Store microchips in BSA-PBS pre-filled wells of a new 96-well plate.
Fill a row of four wells with HPLC-grade water for each microchip.
Keep samples at 4°C for up to two days before imaging.
Prepare the ESEM for wet STEM.
Mount the gaseous secondary electron detector (GSED).
Attach the Peltier stage containing the STEM detector under the sample.
Start the flow of cooling water through the Peltier stage.
Set the temperature of the Peltier stage to 3°C.
Set the stage x-y coordinates to zero.
Adjust the working distance to approximately 6 mm.
Keep the 96-well plate cool on frozen cooling elements in a Styrofoam box.
Take the 96-well plate out of the cooling container and place it near the opened ESEM stage.
Place a new clean room tissue beside the ESEM stage.
Rinse a microchip four times, each for about one second, in HPLC-grade water.
Blot the backside of the rinsed microchip briefly on the clean room tissue.
Place the rinsed and blotted microchip into the precooled ESEM-STEM stage with cells facing up.
Wet the sample surface with 3 µl of cooled HPLC-grade water, avoiding contact with the pipette tip.
Fix the sample in place on the stage.
Add three additional 3 µl water droplets near the sample on the stage.
Close the specimen chamber.
Cycle the pressure five times between 800 and 1,500 Pa within the specimen chamber.
End the cycling at 800 Pa.
Switch on the electron beam (30 kV).
Examine the sample under lowest magnification with both GSED and STEM detectors to locate the microchip window.
Position the SiN membrane window in the center of the image by moving the specimen stage.
Reduce the pressure to 750-720 Pa.
Acquire one or two images showing all cells on the complete window area using the dark field segment of the STEM detector.
Compare these ESEM images with light microscopy images to locate the corners of the SiN window.
Correlate the coordinate frames of both microscopy modalities by comparing magnification, rotation, and possible mirroring.
Locate the same cells in both images.
Select very small dirt particles or a cell region with small features to adjust imaging settings.
Adjust the eucentric height for optimal imaging.
Correct the lens stigmatism for accurate image formation.
Work at a magnification of at least 50,000X.
Use an electron probe current around 0.6 nA for imaging.
Set a pixel-dwell time of 30 µs to capture detailed images.
Use an image size of 1024 x 884 pixels for recording.
Refer to fluorescence images and choose a cell showing strong QD signals for STEM image recording.
Record a STEM overview image of the chosen cell.
Go to a peripheral region where the cell border is visible.
Zoom in to reach 50.000X magnification.
Record images showing individual QDs using pixel dwell times of 20-30 µsec.
Adjust focus and stigmatism for fine adjustments as needed.
Acquire STEM overview images depicting regions recorded with high-magnification as dark rectangles.
Proceed to the next cell of interest.
Start with an overview image.
Record a series of high magnification images.
End with an overview image.
At the end of an ESEM imaging session, increase the pressure to 850-900 Pa before venting the chamber.
